processNotes: The center sequence follows the representative product's historical routing; the operations assigned to those centers are inferred, not an engineering specification.

The BOM does not establish exact frame geometry, stay placement, joint details or fork-retention hardware. The illustration is schematic, and the fork is presented with the frame rather than claimed to be secured to it.
Times are estimates for a lot of one; paint drying or curing duration is not specified.
variantNotes: The representative is Yellow, size 38. The other listed variants are also Yellow: 833 size 40, 834 size 42, 835 size 44 and 836 size 48.
The supplied direct BOMs list the same component IDs and quantities for all five variants, including the same fork and yellow paint; no variant-specific component substitutions are shown.
Use the selected variant's own size-specific geometry and product identity. The snapshot does not supply dimensions or explain how shared component IDs accommodate each size.
The catalog description describes the size 48 variant; it does not establish dimensions for the size 38 representative.

revisions.description: Initial controlled issue for product introduction; established the component list and work-center sequence.
Standardized work-center hand-off notes and separated preparation time from hands-on labor.
Moved variant-selection notes ahead of the first operation to reduce wrong-kit changeovers.
Reordered the Chain Stays receiving check ahead of kit staging; added a missing-part hold point.
Clarified identification of Top Tube; retained the source part number in the point-of-use checklist.
Aligned component count checks with the bill of materials and removed a duplicate sign-off box.
Reformatted shop-floor copies for clearer numbered steps and consolidated inspection comments.
Released the illustrated workstation edition: Frame components and staged fork. Matched numbered component legends to the operating steps and adopted the Manufacturing Hub document layout.

100171.title: Frame components and staged fork
guidance: Arrange 1 EA Head Tube (Product Number HT-8019), 1 EA Down Tube (Product Number DT-2377), 1 EA Seat Tube (Product Number ST-9828) and 1 EA Top Tube (Product Number TO-2301) in an assumed frame jig.

Position 2 EA Chain Stays (Product Number CS-2812) and 4 EA Seat Stays (Product Number SS-2985) for the rear frame arrangement. Their exact placement is not supplied; do not treat the schematic as a joint specification.
Inspect 1 EA ML Fork (Product Number FK-5136) for visible damage and stage it beside the frame as shown in 100171. The view does not specify fork-retention hardware or an installation method.
